Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
13 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.76 -0.99 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 The Financial Times reports ships in the Strait of Hormuz were hit in the worst spate of attacks since the start of the war; Anadolu Ajansı reports six ships targeted in a single day, the highest since the war began.

02 Iran's Nadaja, per Newsquawk, claims a tanker caught fire in the eastern strait; separately, Iranian state media claim an oil tanker attempting an unauthorized crossing caught fire and sustained damage.

03 Brent stood at $105.76, down 0.99% over 24 hours, as of 14:51 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the epicenter of the most intense sustained attack campaign since the war began. The Financial Times reports that ships in the strait have been hit in the worst spate of attacks since the conflict started; Anadolu Ajansı reports that Iranian attacks targeted six ships near the strait in a single day, also the highest figure since the war began. Iran's Nadaja, per Newsquawk, claims a tanker caught fire in the eastern strait after what it called an unauthorized crossing. Separately, Iranian state media claim a second tanker attempting an illegal passage caught fire and sustained damage; those claims originate with Iranian state sources and carry no major wire corroboration in this feed. The IRGC claims it struck another tanker in the strait, per Iranian state media; that claim is being relayed by several outlets but rests on the same originating source. Iran has also warned, per Splash247, that vessels switching off AIS tracking during what it deems unauthorized passages will be treated as hostile. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; the feed carries 40 headlines in the last 24 hours. Brent stood at $105.76, down 0.99% over 24 hours, as of 14:51 UTC. As of 15:22 UTC, 120 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
